questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — length.

options.misconception: Counting push as adding two slots
Counting before the push is applied

questions.explanation: push appends one element, so the list grows from 3 to 4 entries. The length property always counts elements, not the highest index. The printed value is 4, while the alternatives come from counting before the push is applied, counting push as adding two slots and using a zero-based length.
questions.hint: push adds exactly one element to the end of an array.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — splice.
questions.explanation: splice removes two elements starting at index 1 and returns them, leaving 3 elements. Unlike slice, splice changes the original array in place. Carrying the operation through gives 3; common slips include assuming splice leaves the array unchanged and reporting the count of removed items instead.
questions.hint: splice is destructive: the original array shrinks by the removed count.
